epic.text:
Parent initiative: Intelligent Hotel Shopping and Reservation Experience
## Capability summary
Enable guests to submit valid stay criteria and retrieve bookable hotel inventory.
## Business value
Creates qualified traffic for the shopping funnel.
## Scope (user stories)
- 3.1 Search hotels by destination and date range
- 3.2 Validate occupancy and stay criteria
- 3.3 Handle unavailable or failed searches
## Epic acceptance criteria
- All child user stories meet their acceptance criteria and the Definition of Done.
- Negative and error paths for each story are tested and evidenced.
- Required logging is in place and verified free of sensitive data.
- The Product Owner has accepted the capability end to end.
## Dependencies
- Availability service
- Property service
Indicative size: 18 story points across 3 stories (to be refined by the delivery team)
Target planning period: To be agreed at PI / release planning

stories.summary: 3.1 Search hotels by destination and date range
stories.text:
Epic: Epic 1: Search and Availability
## User story
As a guest, I want to search by destination and stay dates so that I can find hotels for my trip.
## Description
Capture destination, check-in, check-out, rooms, adults, and children.
## Acceptance criteria
- Given valid search criteria, when the guest submits the search, then a search request is created and matching available hotels are returned.
- The submitted criteria remain visible and editable on the results page.
- Past check-in dates, check-out dates not after check-in, and missing mandatory fields are rejected with actionable messages.
- A no-availability result explains that no matching inventory was found and allows criteria changes.
## Business rules
- Check-in must precede check-out.
- Occupancy must comply with configured room limits.
- Maximum stay length must be configurable.
## Dependencies
Availability service, Property service
## Logging and audit requirements
- Correlation ID
- Search timestamp
- Destination token or code
- Date range
- Room and occupancy counts
- Result count
- Response status and duration
- Do not log guest names, email addresses, payment data, or raw free-text containing personal data
Story points (indicative): 8 – to be confirmed in refinement
## Notes for refinement
- Use synthetic or approved masked test data only.
- Test cases must trace to this story; defects must link back to it or its test case.

stories.text:
Epic: Epic 1: Search and Availability
## User story
As a guest, I want invalid search inputs identified before submission so that I can correct them quickly.
## Description
Apply client-side and server-side validation consistently.
## Acceptance criteria
- Required fields are clearly identified.
- Invalid combinations return field-level messages.
- Server validation is authoritative when client and server results differ.
- Validation messages are accessible to assistive technology.
## Business rules
- Validation rules must be configurable where market or property rules vary.
## Dependencies
None identified.
## Logging and audit requirements
- Validation rule identifier
- Outcome
- Error category
- Correlation ID; no sensitive field values
Story points (indicative): 5 – to be confirmed in refinement
## Notes for refinement
- Use synthetic or approved masked test data only.
- Test cases must trace to this story; defects must link back to it or its test case.

stories.text:
Epic: Epic 1: Search and Availability
## User story
As a guest, I want a clear response when inventory cannot be found or the search service fails so that I know what to do next.
## Description
Distinguish valid zero-result responses from technical failures.
## Acceptance criteria
- Zero results provide options to alter dates, occupancy, destination, or filters.
- Technical failures display a non-technical message and retry option.
- Repeated submission does not create inconsistent sessions.
## Dependencies
Availability service
## Logging and audit requirements
- Failure category
- Dependency status
- Retry count
- Duration
- Correlation ID
Story points (indicative): 5 – to be confirmed in refinement
## Notes for refinement
- Use synthetic or approved masked test data only.
- Test cases must trace to this story; defects must link back to it or its test case.

coverage.text: All child user stories meet their acceptance criteria and the Definition of Done.
Negative and error paths for each story are tested and evidenced.
Required logging is in place and verified free of sensitive data.
The Product Owner has accepted the capability end to end.
Given valid search criteria, when the guest submits the search, then a search request is created and matching available hotels are returned.
coverage.rationale: Core funnel entry; if it fails, no booking can happen.

coverage.text: The submitted criteria remain visible and editable on the results page.
coverage.rationale: Guests lose context and re-enter criteria.

coverage.text: Past check-in dates, check-out dates not after check-in, and missing mandatory fields are rejected with actionable messages.
coverage.rationale: Three separate validation paths (past date, date order, mandatory fields).

coverage.text: A no-availability result explains that no matching inventory was found and allows criteria changes.
coverage.rationale: A dead end at zero results leads to drop-off.

coverage.text: Occupancy must comply with configured room limits.
coverage.rationale: Room limits are configuration-driven; values not stated in Jira (GAP-01).

coverage.text: Maximum stay length must be configurable.
coverage.rationale: Maximum stay is configuration-driven; value not stated in Jira (GAP-02).
Field-level messages for invalid combinations of occupancy/dates.

coverage.text: Server validation is authoritative when client and server results differ.
coverage.rationale: A client/server mismatch can let invalid searches through.

coverage.text: Validation messages are accessible to assistive technology.
coverage.rationale: Accessibility obligation; full audit beyond key-element lens (GAP-06).

coverage.text: Validation rules must be configurable where market or property rules vary.
coverage.rationale: Market-specific rules; demonstrated with a synthetic market rule (GAP-02).

coverage.text: Zero results provide options to alter dates, occupancy, destination, or filters.
coverage.rationale: Recovery options at zero results; 'filters' not defined in Jira (GAP-09).

coverage.text: Technical failures display a non-technical message and retry option.
coverage.rationale: Technical failure must not leak technical detail and must allow retry.

coverage.text: Repeated submission does not create inconsistent sessions.
coverage.rationale: 'Inconsistent sessions' is not defined in Jira (GAP-07).

gaps.summary: Room limits are 'configured' but no values are given.
gaps.assumption: demo-booking config: max 4 rooms, 3 adults and 2 children per room.

gaps.summary: Maximum stay length is configurable but no default or market values are given.
gaps.assumption: demo-booking config: 30 nights globally, Venice 7 nights (synthetic market rule).

gaps.summary: Logging and audit requirements (correlation ID, duration, retry count...) are not observable through the UI.
gaps.assumption: Not designed as UI cases; candidate for API/log checks outside this PoC.

gaps.summary: Definition of Done and Product Owner acceptance are process sign-offs, not tests.
'Logging verified free of sensitive data' needs log inspection, outside the UI lens.
gaps.assumption: Out of UI scope; listed for Stage 4/API follow-up.

gaps.summary: Only key accessibility semantics are asserted (role=alert summary, aria-invalid, aria-describedby). A full WCAG audit needs tooling such as axe.

gaps.assumption: A double submission produces exactly one search session and one search reference.

gaps.summary: 'A search request is created' has no stated UI evidence.
gaps.assumption: The results page shows a search reference.

gaps.summary: 'Filters' are mentioned but no filter set is defined.
The Availability and Property services are not available; demo-booking simulates them (Atlantis = outage, Reykjavik = zero inventory).
No approved Confluence/BRD pages were supplied; the analysis uses Jira only.
gaps.assumption: Jira descriptions are treated as the approved context.

cases.title: Valid search returns matching available hotels with a search reference
cases.objective: Prove a valid search creates a search request and lists matching available hotels.
preconditions: Guest is on the search page

traces.quote: a search request is created and matching available hotels are returned

steps.action: Enter destination, check-in, check-out, rooms, adults and children
steps.expected: All fields accept the values without error
Results heading shows '3 hotels available in Lisbon'
Three hotel cards are listed and a search reference (S-nnnn) is shown

cases.title: Submitted criteria remain visible and editable on the results page
cases.objective: Prove the guest can see and change the criteria from the results page.
preconditions: A valid search has returned results

traces.quote: The submitted criteria remain visible and editable on the results page

steps.expected: Results are shown

steps.action: Check the search form and criteria summary on the results page
steps.expected: Destination, dates, rooms, adults and children show the submitted values and the inputs are editable

steps.action: Change the price filter and search again
steps.expected: Results update to '1 hotel available in Lisbon' without re-entering other criteria

cases.title: Past check-in date is rejected with an actionable message
cases.objective: Prove a past check-in date cannot be searched.
preconditions: Guest is on the search page

steps.action: Enter criteria with check-in yesterday and submit
steps.expected: Check-in shows 'Check-in date cannot be in the past. Choose today or a later date.' and no results are shown

cases.title: Check-out not after check-in is rejected
cases.objective: Prove the date-order rule is enforced with a field-level message.
preconditions: Guest is on the search page

steps.action: Enter check-out equal to check-in and submit
steps.expected: Check-out shows 'Check-out date must be after the check-in date.'

cases.title: Missing mandatory destination is rejected
preconditions: Guest is on the search page

traces.quote: missing mandatory fields are rejected with actionable messages

steps.expected: Destination shows 'Enter a destination.' and focus moves to it

cases.title: No-availability result explains the outcome and allows criteria changes
cases.objective: Prove a valid zero-result search explains that no inventory matched and lets the guest change criteria.
preconditions: Guest is on the search page

traces.quote: explains that no matching inventory was found and allows criteria changes

steps.expected: Heading 'No hotels found' and text 'We found no matching inventory for these criteria.'

steps.action: Change the destination in the still-visible form and search again
steps.expected: Results heading shows '2 hotels available in Rome'

cases.title: Occupancy above the configured room limit is rejected
cases.objective: Prove occupancy limits from configuration are enforced.

traces.quote: Occupancy must comply with configured room limits

steps.action: Enter 4 adults for 1 room and submit
steps.expected: Adults shows 'A room holds at most 3 adults. Add a room or reduce adults.'

cases.title: Stay longer than the configured maximum is rejected
cases.objective: Prove the configurable maximum stay length is enforced.

traces.quote: Maximum stay length must be configurable

steps.expected: Check-out shows 'Stays in this search are limited to 30 nights. Choose an earlier check-out date.'

cases.title: Required fields are clearly identified
cases.objective: Prove required fields carry a visible marker and are exposed as required to assistive technology.
preconditions: Guest is on the search page

steps.expected: Hint 'Fields marked * are required.' is shown; Destination, Check-in, Check-out, Rooms and Adults are marked * and required

cases.title: Invalid occupancy combination returns a field-level message
cases.objective: Prove invalid combinations are reported against the field at fault.
preconditions: Guest is on the search page

steps.action: Enter 3 children for 1 room and submit
steps.expected: Only Children shows 'A room holds at most 2 children. Add a room or reduce children.'

cases.title: Server-only market rule is enforced when the client accepts the input
cases.objective: Prove server validation is authoritative and market rules are configurable.
preconditions: Venice market max stay per config.limits (GAP-02)

traces.quote: Server validation is authoritative when client and server results differ
configurable where market or property rules vary

steps.action: Search Venice for 8 nights (passes client validation)
steps.expected: Check-out shows 'Stays in Venice are limited to 7 nights. Choose an earlier check-out date.' and no results are shown

cases.title: Validation messages are exposed to assistive technology
cases.objective: Prove error messages are announced and linked to their fields.
preconditions: Guest is on the search page

traces.quote: Validation messages are accessible to assistive technology

steps.expected: An alert summary lists the error; Destination is marked invalid and described by its message

cases.title: Zero results offer options to change dates, occupancy, destination or filters
cases.objective: Prove each recovery option is offered and takes the guest to the matching input.
preconditions: A zero-result search has been made

traces.quote: Zero results provide options to alter dates, occupancy, destination, or filters

steps.expected: Options 'Change dates', 'Change occupancy', 'Change destination' and 'Change filters' are shown
Focus moves to Check-in, Adults, Destination and the price filter respectively

cases.title: Technical failure shows a non-technical message and a retry option
cases.objective: Prove technical failures are distinguished from zero results and are recoverable.
preconditions: Availability service unavailable for the destination (GAP-10)

traces.quote: Technical failures display a non-technical message and retry option

steps.expected: Alert 'We couldn't complete your search' with plain-language text and a 'Try again' button; no error codes shown
The search is retried with the same criteria

cases.title: Rapid repeated submission creates a single consistent search session
cases.objective: Prove repeated submission does not create inconsistent sessions (GAP-07 interpretation).
preconditions: Guest is on the search page

traces.quote: Repeated submission does not create inconsistent sessions

steps.expected: Exactly one results set with one search reference is shown
